welcome.title: Welcome to Clickr
body: Autoclicker for Windows, macOS and Linux with a native input engine.
Use the centre button or the shortcut (F6 by default) to start and stop.
The last configuration you used is restored when the app opens.
The window's X does not quit the app — it goes to the tray. To really quit: tray icon → Quit.
tips: Elapsed time and the real click rate are shown under the counter.
Want a guided preset? Use Wizard mode at the top of this tab.

click.title: Click tab — essentials
body: Interval (ms) + slider: time between actions. The estimated rate is shown below.
Mouse or Key: repeat a mouse button or a key/combination (e.g. E, SPACE, CTRL+C).
Button: L / R / M / 4 / 5 (mouse side buttons).
Type: Single, Double or Hold (kept pressed until you stop).
Position: Cursor (wherever the mouse is) or Fixed point (XY coordinate).
tips: Clickr never clicks on its own window: move the cursor off it for clicks to begin.
Hold releases the button or key when you stop the engine.

run.title: Run tab — limits and system
body: Start delay: wait before the first action; the countdown shows in the centre button.
Jitter ±: random variation of the interval (less “mechanical” clicks).
Click limit / max. duration: stops by itself at N or at the time.
Time fields accept ms, s, min or h — choose the unit next to the value.
Always on top, Compact mode, Start with the system and New-version notice are app preferences (profiles do not change them).

point.title: Point tab — coordinates
body: Set X and Y by hand or use Capture point: the screen dims slightly and your click marks the position.
Position variation ±: each click lands up to N pixels from the point. Return the cursor: the mouse goes back to where it was after the click.
Sequence: list of points with a delay per step. The engine cycles through the list when it is not empty.
“Capture” picks a point on screen and adds it to the list; “+ X/Y” adds the coordinates typed above.
In the list: edit the delay inline, use ↑ ↓ to reorder and × to remove.
tips: Esc cancels the capture. A point lying under the Clickr window is skipped — the footer tells you.

profiles.title: Profiles tab
body: Save the current click configuration under a name. Load applies a profile from the list.
Rename uses the selected profile and the name typed in the field. Delete asks for confirmation.
Export/Import exchanges JSON files with other machines; replacing an existing profile always asks first.
Profiles store only click behaviour. Shortcuts and app preferences are kept separately.
tips: Profiles created in earlier versions keep working as before, including the shortcut they defined.

advanced.title: Adv tab — filter and burst
body: Window filter: acts only if the process and/or title of the focused window match.
Use current window: click, switch to the target window and it is read after 3 seconds.
Burst: N quick clicks, a pause, then repeat — useful for controlled bursts.
While the filter is holding clicks back, the footer shows “outside filter window”.
tips: With the filter on and empty criteria, every action is allowed.

macro.title: Macro tab
body: Record: captures mouse (including the wheel) and keyboard with relative timing.
Play: replays the recording. Repeats sets how many times; Speed makes it faster or slower (1 = original).
Give it a name and use Save / Load / Delete to keep macros between sessions.
Stop interrupts and releases any key or button left pressed.
tips: Set a “Record / stop macro” shortcut in the Keys tab so that clicking the button is not part of the recording.

script.title: Script tab
body: One command per line: click, dclick, move, drag, scroll, wait, key, type and loop N … end.
The “commands” button opens the reference with the syntax of each one.
wait takes a fixed value or a random range (e.g. wait 80-150); key takes combinations (e.g. key CTRL+C).
Limits: up to 500 lines, loops from 1 to 1000, at most 2 nested loops.
The text is kept for next time; while running, the current line is shown.
tips: Syntax errors tell you the line number.

schedule.title: Schedule tab
body: Choose the local date/time and what to start: auto-click with the current settings, a saved profile, the loaded macro or the script.
Repeat: once, every day at the same time, or every interval.
The schedule is saved: recurring schedules come back when you reopen the app.
Cancel removes the active schedule.
tips: Clickr must be running (it can stay in the tray) for the schedule to fire.

safety.title: Responsible use
body: Use only where you have authorization.
In online games / anti-cheat, an autoclicker may violate terms and cause a ban.
Clickr does not bypass anti-cheat. Admin windows may ignore input if Clickr is not elevated.
tips: You are responsible for how you use the software.

keys.title: Keys tab
body: Each action has its own global shortcut: Start / stop, Stop everything, Capture point at cursor and Record / stop macro.
Click a shortcut and press the combination — Ctrl, Alt, Shift and Win are allowed (e.g. Ctrl+Alt+F6). Esc cancels; × removes.
Toggle: one press starts, another stops. Hold: clicks only while the shortcut is held down.
“Stop everything” halts auto-click, macro, script and capture at once.
tips: On Windows the shortcut is not passed on to the focused program. Prefer function keys or combinations with a modifier.

mouse_buttons.title: Mouse buttons (L R M 4 5)
body: L — left button (the “normal” click).
R — right button (context menu).
M — middle button (usually the wheel pressed).
4 and 5 — side buttons (back/forward), if your mouse has them.

click_type.title: Click type
body: Single — one click at a time, at the interval pace.
Double — two quick clicks each cycle (like double-clicking an icon).
Hold — keeps the button pressed until you stop Clickr (not repeated clicking).

interval.title: Interval and CPS
body: Interval is the pause between one click and the next, in milliseconds (ms). 1000 ms = 1 second.
E.g.: 80 ms ≈ 12.5 clicks per second (CPS).
Smaller numbers = faster. Start slower when testing.

position.title: Where to click
body: Cursor — clicks where the mouse is at the time (you can move while it runs).
Fixed point — always the same screen coordinate (X, Y).
Capture point — the screen dims; click the desired place (Esc cancels). Works on all monitors.

limits.title: What are limits?
body: Optional stops so Clickr does not run forever. You can leave everything empty/zero and adjust later on the Run tab.

delay.title: Start delay
body: Wait time before the first click, after you hit Start.
Useful so you can press Start and still return to the right game or window.
E.g.: 2000 ms = waits 2 seconds, then starts clicking.

jitter.title: Jitter (±)
body: Random variation on the interval so clicks are not 100% robotic.
E.g.: interval 80 ms and jitter 10 → each pause is between ~70 and ~90 ms.
0 = no variation (fixed rhythm).

max_clicks.title: Click limit
body: Maximum number of clicks. When reached, Clickr stops on its own.
Empty field (∞) = no quantity limit.

max_duration.title: Max duration
body: Maximum time the engine stays active, in milliseconds.
E.g.: 10000 = stops automatically after 10 seconds.
Empty field (∞) = no time limit.

profile.title: Profile (preset)
body: A name to store this configuration and reuse later.
Lives on the Profiles tab (load, export, import).
Afterwards you can change button, interval, etc. on Click / Run / Point without redoing the Wizard.
